training.store: v3 gpt2_wikitext store: first 5M tokens of WikiText-103-v1 train, one document per 128-token sequence, padding excluded
training.centering: x - train mean (raw scale, no rescaling)
training.init_seed: torch.manual_seed(seed) and v3 BaseSAE tied init with Generator(seed)
training.decoder: rows renormalized to unit norm after every Adam step
training.bypass: x - (x.v1) v1 with the train PC1 before encoding (bypass condition only)

protocol.alive: calibration-alive = fired at least once on the calibration split. The bridge uses the FROZEN alive ids from the grid evaluator (identical sets, checked); fresh_alive is the bridge re-count on its own bfloat16 calibration pass.
protocol.importance: signed single-feature zero-ablation dCE vs the unmodified model ("model" baseline), token-weighted over the ranking split; every calibration-alive feature evaluated (no screen)
protocol.top50: top_ids: the 50 calibration-alive features with the largest dCE on the named split; ties broken by feature index
protocol.sharing: for source seed a and each other seed b in the same (condition, beta): best = max over b's calibration-alive decoder rows of the signed cosine with a's decoder row. top50_pairwise_sharing(a) = fraction of (other seed, selected feature) pairs with best >= 0.7. Reported sharing = mean over the 5 source seeds. dictwide uses all of a's calibration-alive features instead of the top 50.
protocol.l0: bridge fidelity(): total nonzero codes over the split's valid tokens / number of valid tokens (no row cap)
protocol.fvu: fvu_total = sum||x - xhat||^2 / sum||x - mean_eval||^2; fvu_content (fvu_perp) = same on the complement of the train PC1; w1 = PC1 share of evaluation variance; identity fvu_total = w1*fvu_pc1 + (1-w1)*fvu_content holds to <3e-18
protocol.uncertainty: sharing: article-resampled paired bootstrap (bridge paired_contrasts, ~1000 draws). L0/FVU/alive: across the 5 seeds (mean, SD, Student-t 95%); beta effects are PAIRED by seed (identical init seed and data order across beta).

geometry.definition:
GPT-2 B1 companion geometry: PC1 alignment of calibration-alive atoms and cross-seed sharing by alignment band.

Inputs: the 40 bridge calibration files (decoder rows, frozen calibration-alive mask, alignment = cos^2(decoder, train PC1))
and BRIDGE_RESULTS per-seed top-50 selected ids (test split, model baseline, dCE).
Bands follow exp_b2_l1_phase.py (the Pythia sweep's own definitions): canonical cos^2 >= 0.3, tiling band 0.01 <= cos^2 < 0.3,
content cos^2 < 0.01. Sharing threshold 0.7 on the signed max cosine against another seed's calibration-alive atoms (as in the bridge).

protocol.training: v3 get_sae/train_sae: TopKL1SAE, centered raw activations (x - store mean), 20,000 steps, batch 4,096, Adam 3e-4, decoder renormalized after each step; store = first 5M tokens of WikiText-103-v1 train, one document per 128-token sequence, padding excluded, float16
protocol.archived_l0_field_origin: l0_measured[seed] = float(rates.sum()) with rates, alive = io.alive(sae, adir) (pc1_v3/v3/common/io_utils.py): for i in range(0, 100000, 8192) encodes acts[i:i+8192] with no clamp (13 slices, 106,496 rows) and divides counts by n = 100,000

archived_other_l0_fields.l0_batch: l1_pressure(): mean nonzeros over 4 random batches of 4,096 rows (rng seed 777) drawn from the whole store; seed 42 checkpoint only
archived_other_l0_fields.l0_train_log_stale: training log at step 19,000, seed 42 only

protocol.archived_fvu_origin: fvu = extra["log"][-1]["fvu"] = training-batch FVU at step 19,000 for seed 42 (checkpoint train log); not an evaluation
protocol.sharing: single ordered pair: seed 42 reference vs seed 137; importance = zero-ablation dCE for seed 42 over 64 WikiText-103 validation sequences (first 64 non-empty lines, padded to 128, pad fraction 0.44), screened to the top 1,500 alive atoms by E[z^2]; top-50 = highest dCE among seed-42 alive atoms (alive from the unclamped routine, rate > 1e-3); shared if signed max cosine against all seed-137 decoder rows >= 0.7; no held-out split, no uncertainty

recompute.validation: reproduced_old_routine vs archived l0_measured: max abs difference 0.00158691 over 26 checkpoints
recompute.corrected_definition: corrected_l0 = sum over rows r in [0, 100000) of #nonzero(sae.encode(acts[r] - mean)) / 100000; final batch clamped; same store, centering, float32 encode and row order as io.alive

identical_in_code: loss form: mean over batch of (sum over d of squared error) + beta * mean over batch of (sum over latents of |z|)  [grid: train_objective_grid.py loss=mse+beta*z.abs().sum(-1).mean(); native: pc1night/model.py loss_parts (weights=1, loss_axis=1 for the beta arms)]
activation: z = TopK_k(ReLU((x - b_dec) W_enc + b_enc)), k=64, TopK applied after ReLU on pre-activations  [v3 saes.py TopKSAE.encode; pc1night model.py SAE.encode]
tied initialization from a CPU Generator(seed): W_dec rows unit-normalized Gaussian, W_enc = W_dec transpose, zero biases, learned b_dec
Adam lr 3e-4, betas 0.9/0.999, eps 1e-8; 20,000 steps; batch 4,096; width 3,072 (GPT-2); site transformer.h[6]
beta enters only as a constant multiplier of the same L1 term (native beta_0.03/0.1/0.3 arms: constant schedule)

different_in_code.native: (x - train mean) / s, s = sqrt(mean_train ||x - mean||^2) = 274.83 for GPT-2 (pc1night data.py reference(); reference.json)
different_in_code.consequence: per-row MSE scales by 1/s^2 and code magnitudes (hence L1) by 1/s, so at a fixed dictionary the penalty-to-reconstruction ratio at the same numeric beta is ~s times larger in native units

different_in_code.measured: engaged at 2.4% of logged steps (step 1 onward; median pre-clip norm 0.008): not active in steady state

different_in_code.grid: renormalize rows after each Adam step (v3 renorm_decoder)
different_in_code.native: project the W_dec gradient onto the tangent of the unit sphere (tangent_grad) before the step AND renormalize after (constrain)

different_in_code.grid: v3 store: first 5M tokens of WikiText-103-v1 train, one document per 128-token sequence, no BOS; rows drawn uniformly with replacement (default_rng(20260906))
different_in_code.native: pc1night harvest (BOS kept in the LM context; 128-token sequences), 5,000,017 train rows; superblocks of 32x4096 indices drawn with replacement (order seed 20260908)

different_in_code.grid: bridge (pc1next): bfloat16 LM, article splits, frozen calibration-alive masks
different_in_code.native: pc1night evaluation: population-resolved FVU on its own test rows (not directly comparable numbers)

native_gpt2.units: native trainer units: inputs (x - train mean)/scale, scale = 274.83 (reference.json)

native_top50_sharing_beta03_preliminary.source: native_prelim/LM_SUMMARY.json (preliminary collect; dictionaries retain ~51 alive atoms, so top-50 sharing is nearly degenerate)

implementation_comparison.attribution: The only code difference that changes how strong a given numeric beta is, is the native global input rescaling. Measured at the start of training (identical-form objectives, beta=0.3) the penalty/reconstruction ratio is 0.851 native vs 0.0021 grid; at the beta=0 solutions the L1 cost per unit beta relative to MSE is 219 native vs 0.98 grid (x224). Native L0 collapses within the first 500-2,000 steps (0.72 at step 500, 0.04 by step 2,000 at beta=0.3). This establishes that equal numeric beta values are not equal penalties across the two trainers; it does not isolate the rescaling from the other listed differences (decoder tangent projection, store, sampling), which were not ablated.
